item.title: Floyd Mayweather Fawns Over Donald Trump Onstage At Midterm Rally
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Floyd Mayweather joined Donald Trump in Arizona as the president rallied support for Republican candidates ahead of Election Day.
item.content:encoded:
Floyd Mayweather backed President Donald Trump onstage at an Arizona rally on Wednesday, October 14, adding his voice to the president’s push for Republican wins in next month’s midterm elections.

The boxer joined Trump at Laughlin/Bullhead International Airport in Bullhead City. He flew from Las Vegas with the president aboard Air Force One.

Trump introduced Mayweather by praising his defense and linking that style to the boxer’s looks. He also highlighted Mayweather’s earnings before inviting him to the microphone. He referred to the boxer by his “Money” nickname.

“He looks so good. Who would believe he’s a fighter? He looks so good. He doesn’t have a mark, that’s why I’d rather be a great defensive fighter,” President Trump gushed.

Mayweather then said, “we couldn’t have chose a better president twice than Donald Trump.”

He thanked those who came out, praised the United States and recalled representing the country at the 1996 Olympic Games.

“America is the best country in the world. If I died and came back a million times, I will always choose America. We couldn’t have chose a better president twice than Donald Trump. So, it’s all about keeping this country strong, and it’s all about us sticking together and believing one another. America is the best country in the world,” Floyd Mayweather told the crowd.

He ended his brief remarks by urging Americans to stick together and believe in one another.

Afterward, Trump thanked Mayweather and dwelled on his unbeaten 50-0 record, noting that he had faced top opponents throughout his boxing career.

Combat sports outlet Happy Punch shared a clip of his remarks that evening.

Mayweather also appeared at the Republican Jewish Coalition’s 2025 leadership summit in Las Vegas. He accepted its World Champion for Israel Award and spoke about his support for Israel.

Mayweather had voiced his support for Trump well before this campaign stop. He also attended Trump’s first presidential inauguration in January 2017.

During a February 2025 appearance on Fox Business’s “Making Money with Charles Payne,” he praised Trump’s work as president and his business background.

AllHipHop reported at the time that 50 Cent mocked the interview in an Instagram post.

“LOL YO you know how, when you’re in school and a kid eats the crayons,” 50 Cent wrote in the caption. “Now you see what happens when they grow up. Spell BEST PRESIDENT champ! LOL.”

The Arizona stop placed him alongside a recent string of boxers who joined Trump on the road. Mike Tyson appeared at a rally on October 9 in Syracuse, New York.

Jake Paul joined an October 12 event in Youngstown, Ohio. Mayweather’s appearance made three boxers at three Trump rallies in six days.

In Bullhead City, Trump sought votes for U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs, the Republican challenging Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs. Biggs took the stage and urged the crowd to support Republicans throughout the ticket.

The visit came while early voting was underway in Arizona. Races for governor, attorney general and the U.S. House were on the November 3 ballot.

item.title: Eminem Stays On Kid Rock Album As Lil Wayne Takes Over “7 Sins”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Eminem remained on Kid Rock's gospel album as Lil Wayne took over "7 Sins" and the Detroit rapper moved to "Heal My Faith."
item.content:encoded:
Eminem kept his spot on Kid Rock’s gospel album as Lil Wayne took over “7 Sins,” the song at the center of a clash over the Detroit stars’ politics.

Kid Rock shared the change on October 14, then posted a new tracklist for Halfway 2 Jesus. The image listed Lil Wayne on the third song, “7 Sins,” and Eminem on the fifth, “Heal My Faith.”

Kid Rock used a new video to address fans who didn’t want him to work with Eminem. He first teased that those critics might be glad to hear Eminem was off “7 Sins.”

He then named Lil Wayne as the new guest before sharing the other half of the news

“Eminem is still on the album. He’s just on another song now, called ‘Heal My Faith,'” Kid Rock said.

Kid Rock’s ties to Eminem went back long before this record. AllHipHop’s earlier report noted Eminem’s guest spot on “F#ck Off” from Kid Rock’s 1998 album Devil Without A Cause. Kid Rock later appeared in Eminem’s “Berzerk” video.

The first look at “7 Sins” had brought that friendship into a fresh debate.

On October 5, critics criticized Eminem’s choice to work with Kid Rock, who backed Donald Trump. Eminem had appeared at a Kamala Harris campaign rally in Detroit in 2024, putting the pair on opposite sides of that race.

Kid Rock told Fox News earlier this month that he and Eminem had agreed to keep politics from dividing their friendship.

In the new video, Kid Rock again stood by his choice to work with people who held different views.

He said the guests, musicians, songwriters and engineers who made the album did not all think alike. He framed that right to hold different views as part of what made the country great.

Halfway 2 Jesus was scheduled to arrive on October 17, the date in Kid Rock’s X announcement.

item.title: Lord Conrad Drops Highly Anticipated Single “Rising Empire”
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Lord Conrad blends 80s synthwave, hip-hop, trap, and heavy 808s on “Rising Empire,” a GTA 6-inspired release fueled by Vice City nightlife, luxury, ambition, and cinematic gaming culture.
item.content:encoded:
Neon nights. Luxury cars. Champagne. Heavy 808s. The rise of an empire.

Enter a world of 80s synthwave, distorted electric guitars, modern hip-hop, and trap, where retro neon aesthetics collide with luxury, ambition, and the streets of Vice City.

Rising Empire is a GTA 6-inspired musical experience by Lord Conrad, capturing the energy of Vice City, cinematic open-world gaming, neon nightlife, and the rise of a new generation.

From the neon streets of GTA6 to the real-world financial markets, the empire-building mindset goes beyond the game.

With the gaming industry evolving and the spotlight on the future of Grand Theft Auto VI, the market keeps its eyes on Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ: TTWO), the company behind the Grand Theft Auto franchise, alongside the broader Nasdaq and the business of interactive entertainment.

Ambition. Innovation. Risk. The next big move.

Rising Empire — where gaming culture, financial ambition, and music collide.

THE RISING EMPIRE EXPERIENCE

GTA 6 / GTA VI Inspired

Vice City & Neon Nights

Luxury Cars & Midnight Drives

Champagne & Luxury Lifestyle

80s Synthwave & Distorted Guitars

Modern Hip-Hop, Trap & Heavy 808s

This is more than a vibe. It’s a statement.

Lord Conrad is rising. The empire starts now.

item.title: AKA Murder Trial Witness Says Rapper Seemed To Avoid Someone Before Shooting
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: AKA's murder trial heard a witness describe his final embrace with Tibz and the desperate attempts to save his friend's life.
item.content:encoded:
AKA appeared to be trying to avoid someone moments before he was killed, a witness told the Durban High Court Wednesday as the murder trial turned to his final embrace with Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane.

The witness said the friends hugged outside Wish restaurant for longer than usual. He believed AKA had spotted someone from his past and did not want to be noticed. As they moved around during the embrace, Tibz could get a better look in that person’s direction.

“I think AKA had noticed someone from his past and he did not want that person to notice him,” the witness testified, SABC News reported.

That was the witness’s interpretation of the exchange. He said the pair then stopped hugging and shook hands. As he turned toward the group’s vehicle, he heard a bang, which he initially took for fireworks, and sought cover.

When the group looked back out, AKA had been hit and showed no movement while Tibz tried to crawl away. The witness described the panic that followed as friends called for help and watched Tibz lose blood.

Paramedics tried several times to revive Tibz, the witness said. Both men were declared dead at the scene after the February 10, 2023 shooting on Durban’s Florida Road.

The court also heard from two people who sat in a park across from the restaurant. They testified from another courtroom because they feared being identified and facing the seven defendants in open court.

One recalled a man using his phone nearby, then heading toward a bus stop shortly before gunshots. The witness said two men wearing masks and hats ran toward the park, got into a car and fled.

One carried a gun, but he could not see their faces.

A second witness gave a similar account and said he had noticed the masked men before the shooting.

Under cross-examination, defense lawyer Simphiwe Mlotshwa questioned why his police statement omitted his description of one man’s larger build. The witness said officers had not asked him to describe the men.

The new evidence follows earlier testimony about the shooting’s aftermath and challenges to the state’s firearm evidence.

All seven defendants pleaded not guilty when the trial opened on October 5. They face charges including murder, conspiracy, attempted murder and firearm offenses.

The trial continues Thursday, October 15, with prosecutors expected to call their 14th witness.

item.title: Former Bodyguard Challenges Diddy Prison Fight Reports, Calls Cap
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Diddy's former bodyguard Roger Bonds claims sources inside Fort Dix are capping about the mogul's fight with a notorious Jamaican kingpin.
item.content:encoded:
What in the world is going on with Diddy behind those prison walls?

I have to tell you, this story keeps getting stranger, and now somebody who knows Sean “Diddy” Combs personally is speaking out. And this is not somebody who has been particularly friendly toward the former Bad Boy boss in recent years.

I’m talking about Roger Bonds.

For those who don’t know, Bonds is Diddy’s former longtime bodyguard. He worked closely with the mogul and was around during some of the most controversial periods of his life, including his relationship with Cassie Ventura. Bonds has since become an outspoken critic of his former employer, publicly discussing allegations of abusive behavior that he says he witnessed.

So, when somebody like that starts challenging reports about Diddy getting attacked in prison, I’m going to pay attention.

As you already know, reports surfaced that Diddy was transported out of FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey for medical treatment following an apparent head injury. TMZ reported that an ambulance left the prison early Saturday morning and that Diddy returned before sunrise.

Then came reports connecting the medical emergency to a confrontation with Christopher “Dudus” Coke, the notorious Jamaican drug kingpin associated with the Shower Posse.

Yes, THAT Shower Posse.

Now, Bonds is offering another version of what allegedly happened.

According to Bonds, who claims to have sources inside Fort Dix, Diddy was not struck in the head during the encounter. He says there was a relatively minor skirmish between the two men, but the situation was not nearly as dramatic as some reports have suggested.

Essentially, Bonds claims the two men had a confrontation and eventually went their separate ways.

However, Diddy’s separate way apparently included a trip outside the prison for medical attention.

Now, what exactly happened there? Your guess is as good as mine.

We know there have been reports of a medical emergency, but the precise circumstances surrounding the reported injury remain disputed. Bonds’ account has not been independently verified, and the connection between the confrontation and the medical treatment has not been conclusively established through publicly available medical records or an official prison statement.

Nevertheless, Bonds offered some perspective that I found particularly revealing.

Diddy’s Alleged Prison Privileges May Be Creating Enemies

According to Bonds, there’s a bigger problem developing inside Fort Dix, and it has to do with the difference between somebody serving a relatively short sentence and somebody who has spent decades behind bars.

Think about that.

Diddy is a celebrity who lived an extraordinarily luxurious lifestyle for most of his adult life. He had the mansions, private jets, expensive clothing, exotic vacations and everything else that comes with being one of the wealthiest figures in Hip-Hop.

Now he’s in federal prison.

But there have been reports alleging that certain luxuries have followed him inside.

We’ve heard stories about cellphones, alcohol, massages and other alleged unauthorized privileges. These claims have generated plenty of headlines, although the specific allegations and any resulting disciplinary actions have not all been independently confirmed.

Bonds suggested that this type of behavior can create serious problems for people who have been incarcerated for much longer periods.

Why?

Because when somebody attracts attention to what’s happening inside a prison, the consequences can affect everybody.

Imagine being locked up for 20 or 30 years. You’ve developed routines, relationships and ways of surviving that environment. Then a celebrity comes through, allegedly enjoys privileges other inmates may not have, and suddenly prison officials start paying closer attention to everything.

That can disrupt the entire environment.

And as Bonds essentially explained it, these men aren’t just passing through. This is where they live.

That statement stuck with me.

For Diddy, Fort Dix is a temporary stop in what has become a remarkable fall from grace. His projected release date has been reported as March 2028, although that remains subject to change.

For some of these other men, prison is their reality for decades.

That’s an entirely different mindset.

And if Bonds’ interpretation is accurate, the resentment may have less to do with Diddy personally and more to do with the disruption surrounding his presence.

Now, I’m not saying that makes any alleged violence acceptable. It doesn’t.

But I can understand how tensions might develop in an environment where people have very little control over their daily lives.

Who Is Christopher “Dudus” Coke?

The other name reportedly connected to this situation is Christopher “Dudus” Coke, and that’s a serious piece of history.

Coke is a former Jamaican drug kingpin who led the Shower Posse, a notorious criminal organization with roots in Kingston’s Tivoli Gardens community. The group became associated with international drug trafficking and violence, particularly during the crack cocaine era.

Coke’s influence in Jamaica was so significant that efforts to arrest and extradite him in 2010 helped trigger a deadly confrontation between Jamaican security forces and armed supporters in Kingston.

He eventually pleaded guilty in the United States to federal racketeering-related and assault conspiracy charges and was sentenced to 23 years in prison in 2012.

This is not somebody whose name ordinarily appears in celebrity gossip.

And that’s part of what makes these reports so unsettling.

We’re talking about two men from completely different worlds who reportedly crossed paths inside the federal prison system.

One helped define an era of Hip-Hop and became a global entertainment mogul. The other became internationally notorious through organized crime.

And now their names are being connected through reports of a prison confrontation.

You couldn’t make this stuff up.

But here’s the important distinction: the history of Coke and the Shower Posse is documented. The exact circumstances of his reported encounter with Diddy remain a separate matter, and conflicting accounts should not be confused with confirmed facts.

Roger Bonds Has His Own History With Diddy

Another reason I’m paying attention to Bonds is his complicated relationship with Diddy.

Remember, this is a man who previously worked closely with the mogul and later became one of his public critics.

Bonds has spoken about alleged incidents involving Cassie Ventura and Diddy, and his name surfaced in connection with Cassie’s 2023 civil lawsuit.

He has made it clear through previous interviews that he has serious issues with his former employer.

That’s why I find his latest comments noteworthy.

He isn’t somebody who has been running around defending Diddy at every opportunity.

Yet, according to his account, the reports of a serious physical attack may be exaggerated.

Does that make Bonds correct? Absolutely not.

Does it make his perspective worth examining? I think so.

The fact that he claims to have sources inside Fort Dix also raises questions. Who are these people? How close were they to the alleged incident? Are they reporting firsthand knowledge or simply repeating what they’ve heard?

Those are things we still don’t know.

And until we do, I think it’s important to avoid treating any single version as the final word.

item.title: Keion White Shooting After Reported Lil Baby Dispute Leads To Four Arrests
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Keion White's shooting case reached four arrests as police named more suspects in the nightclub violence linked to a Lil Baby dispute.
item.content:encoded:
Keion White’s shooting case reached four arrests as San Francisco police announced three more suspects Wednesday. The February nightclub shooting followed a reported argument involving Lil Baby.

The October 14 update added Marquis Davis, Antoine Washington and Curtis Green to the case against Gregory Walker, whose arrest AllHipHop covered last week.

Cops arrested all four men between October 7 and October 9, then brought Walker and Green to San Francisco’s jail on October 12.

Prosecutors filed different gun charges against the two men now in local custody. Walker, 36, faced assault with a semiautomatic firearm and three counts tied to a felon carrying or possessing a gun. Prosecutors alleged that he fired the gun and caused great bodily injury.

The district attorney’s office said Walker and a second man awaiting charges both fired guns at the party, leaving White wounded.

The office did not name that second alleged shooter in its release.

Green, 35, faced three misdemeanor counts for allegedly brandishing a gun, carrying a concealed gun and carrying a loaded gun in public. District Attorney Brooke Jenkins’ office said it would ask a judge to keep Walker jailed without bail, citing a threat to public safety.

Police called the case Operation D-Line.

It took more than 50 search warrants and help from more than 250 officers and other personnel across the country. Cops said the searches turned up guns and nearly 15 pounds of drugs.

“What started as a shooting investigation expanded rapidly,” San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said.

Atlanta police arrested Davis, 38, at his home, where officers said they found an illegal gun and MDMA, methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl.

Police arrested Washington, 36, in Stockton and said they seized a loaded gun, more than 120 oxycodone pills and $6,691. Irvine was the site of Green’s arrest on October 7. Los Angeles police arrested Walker two days later.

White was hosting a private Super Bowl party downstairs at Dahlia’s in San Francisco when he was shot in the ankle early February 9.

The San Francisco Standard reviewed a police report in which a witness said Lil Baby’s group tried to enter White’s event. The witness described an argument between White and the rapper, then heard shots while upstairs seeking help from club managers. He told police he did not know who fired.

White underwent surgery and returned to play for the 49ers this season.

Police worked to bring Davis and Washington to San Francisco, where they had not yet announced charges. The shooting investigation remained open, and officers asked other witnesses to come forward.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Feds Fight To Keep Lil Durk Co-Defendants’ Stalking Convictions
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Lil Durk’s co-defendants faced a new government push to uphold their stalking convictions after the jury’s split verdict.
item.content:encoded:
Federal prosecutors asked a judge to keep Lil Durk’s co-defendants’ stalking convictions in place in a new October 14 filing.

The 31-page response asked U.S. District Judge Michael Fitzgerald to reject post-trial requests from Deandre “DeDe” Wilson and David “Browneyez” Lindsey.

The men sought acquittal or a new trial on charges tied to the killing of Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson.

The new filing addressed a key defense claim about the plot targeting Tyquian “Quando Rondo” Bowman. The defense argued that a secret effort to kill someone failed to meet the federal rules for stalking because the target did not know he was being followed.

AllHipHop previously reported that DeDe’s lawyer argued the evidence showed a surprise attack and failed to prove stalking. The government’s new response argued that hidden acts could still form the required pattern of conduct.

Prosecutors wrote:

“First, defendants’ argument that their premeditated — and largely clandestine — stalking and murder scheme is not covered by the federal stalking statute ignores the plain text of the statute and binding caselaw. The statute defines ‘course of conduct’ as a pattern of conduct composed of two or more acts — none of which needs to be known to the victims. The statute also criminalizes such conduct when it ‘causes, attempts to cause, or would be reasonably expected to cause’ substantial emotional distress. Defendants’ multi-day stalking and murder scheme that caused Mr. Robinson’s death and severe emotional distress to Bowman clearly falls within the scope of the statute.”

The brief pointed to travel records, phone data, video and witness accounts. Prosecutors argued those records showed a plan to track Quando Rondo across Los Angeles before the August 19, 2022 shooting. Quando Rondo survived. His cousin Lul Pab was killed.

The government also responded to the defense’s claim that Lul Pab was not the intended target. Prosecutors argued that following an occupied SUV and firing into it supported the stalking count involving his death.

The brief also stated:

“Third, a reasonable jury could — and did — find that the conspirators intended to stalk Mr. Robinson in addition to Bowman. The evidence proved the conspirators knew Bowman, Robinson, and others were inside the vehicle, and their murder plan involved using a machinegun and other firearms to indiscriminately fire at the victims’ vehicle. This and other evidence presented at trial sufficiently established the conspirators’ intent to kill, injure, harass, or intimidate everyone inside of the vehicle, including Mr. Robinson.”

Browneyez’s request for a new trial raised other issues, including being tried with the other defendants, the use of certain evidence and the judge’s jury instructions. The government also opposed those claims.

The challenge followed the September 11 verdict.

The jury acquitted Lil Durk on all five counts at that trial. DeDe and Browneyez were convicted of three stalking counts, but both were acquitted of the murder-for-hire charges.

Their lawyers had signaled that the fight would continue.

item.title: Kanye West’s Pockets Take $180K Hit In Battle With Handyman
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Kanye West faced another $181,433.93 bill in Tony Saxon's Malibu mansion lawsuit after a judge awarded attorney fees and costs.
item.content:encoded:
Kanye West faced another $181,433.93 bill after a judge awarded legal fees and costs to the former worker who sued him over his gutted Malibu mansion.

Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Brock Hammond ordered the payment on October 13, adding to Tony Saxon’s $140,000 jury award from March. Rolling Stone, which obtained the ruling, reported $147,000 in attorney fees and $34,433.93 in costs.

The new award exceeded the damages Saxon won at trial, though it fell well short of the $1.23 million his lawyers sought. Ye’s side had fought the fee request entirely and asked that any award be capped at $59,425, MyNewsLA reported.

The dispute over that bill followed a mixed verdict. Jurors awarded Saxon $100,000 for past and future medical expenses and $40,000 for past pain and suffering. They rejected his wrongful-termination claim and declined to award punitive damages.

Hammond heard arguments about fees on October 7 before taking the matter under review. Saxon’s team said the case required work from three attorneys and a paralegal and cost their firm more than $300,000.

Ye’s lawyers argued that the request was far too high given how few of Saxon’s claims succeeded.

The fight began in 2021, when Saxon worked at the beachfront house. Saxon said he was promised $20,000 a week to oversee the project and also served as a caretaker and security guard.

His lawsuit alleged unsafe conditions, unpaid compensation and injuries he suffered while working there.

The renovation went far beyond changing the decor.

A New Yorker investigation documented the removal of bathrooms, windows and other basic features through interviews, photographs and messages. Saxon described recruiting a crew and living at the property as demolition proceeded.

The city also confirmed it issued stop-work orders because construction took place without permits.

Ye bought the Tadao Ando-designed home for $57.3 million, then sold the stripped property for $21 million in 2024. Selling the house did not end the employment dispute or the later fight over the cost of litigating it.

Saxon’s attorney, Ron Zambrano, credited Hammond with reconsidering an initially lower amount.

“I respect Judge Hammond’s openness to consider my argument why his initial assessment was perhaps missing a critical point,” Zambrano said.

He still said the firm’s work deserved more. Ye’s spokesman cast the reduced award as a defeat for Saxon’s side.

The rapper is appealing the earlier $140,000 judgment.

item.title: Eminem’s Ex-Wife Kim Mathers Loses Bid To Drop Court-Ordered Rehab
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Kim Mathers lost her bid to remove inpatient treatment from her release terms as a Michigan judge delayed her court hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Kim Mathers, Eminem’s ex-wife, lost a bid to leave jail without returning to court-ordered rehab at a Michigan hearing on October 14.

Judge William H. Hackel III denied her lawyer Camilla Barkovic’s request to restore bond terms a magistrate had approved, WDIV reported.

Under those terms, Mathers could leave jail without going back to treatment. She appeared by Zoom before the 42-2 District Court in New Baltimore.

When Barkovic asked whether Mathers could still leave jail for inpatient care, Hackel confirmed that she could. That option had already been part of his bond terms before Wednesday’s hearing.

Hackel gave Barkovic more time to file multiple motions on her client’s behalf and agreed to delay the probable cause conference.

AllHipHop previously reported that Hackel sent Mathers back to Macomb County Jail on October 7 after a dispute over her departure from treatment.

The Macomb County Prosecutor’s Office traced the October 7 dispute to Mathers’ August 26 exit from Sacred Heart Rehabilitation Center. It said warrants followed her departure from the center, where Hackel had ordered her to get care.

On October 2, Mathers appeared before Magistrate Genevieve L. Taylor, who canceled the warrants and set a $5,000 bond with house arrest, prosecutors said. Hackel ruled five days later that the magistrate lacked authority to change his order, and returned Mathers to jail.

The fight over her bond involves three cases. Prosecutors said Mathers pleaded no contest on May 11 to impaired driving and failure to report an accident. Those misdemeanor counts carry maximum jail terms of 93 days and 90 days, respectively.

Police told CBS Detroit that she hit a parked car in Chesterfield on May 13; no one was hurt. Prosecutors charged her with third-offense drunk driving, a felony that carries up to five years in prison.

The state also brought two felony counts for an alleged clash with police on July 11. One count says she hurt an officer; the other involves assaulting, resisting or obstructing police. The two counts carry up to four years and two years in prison.

Hackel told the court, “the bond stays as is.”

item.title: Daejon Love’s Fake 49ers Story Heads To Netflix’s “Untold”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Daejon Love's Netflix documentary will center women affected by the alleged romance scam as his federal case moves toward trial.
item.content:encoded:
Daejon Love’s alleged fake NFL romance scam is headed to Netflix, where a new “Untold” film will focus on the women caught up in the case.

The film is called “Untold: Wide Deceiver,” The Hollywood Reporter revealed. It will be “told firsthand from those affected by the scam,” with a production source saying the women and their experiences will drive the story.

That focus puts the women behind Love’s viral 49ers story in the spotlight. Federal prosecutors say he used claims of football fame, wealth and love to sell them on deals that did not exist.

Federal prosecutors arrested Love and Taylor Jamie Chan at Boise Airport on August 24. The Justice Department said the alleged scheme involved 26 identified victims and about $1.3 million.

Prosecutors charged both men with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

The feds say Love met most of the women through dating apps. He claimed to be a San Francisco 49ers player or a rich real estate investor. Chan allegedly posed as his financial adviser, joined calls and sent messages that made the deals seem real.

The pitch reached beyond football.

The feds say Love promised some women a future together, showed fake bank balances and urged those without cash to take out loans. Prosecutors said women who asked too many questions or ran out of money were then blocked.

The number of possible victims grew after the arrests. As AllHipHop reported in September, the FBI said 35 more women had come forward. The FBI was still checking those claims at that time. Those women were in addition to the 26 described in the first complaint.

Rachel Anderson said she met Love on Bumble in June 2024, when he introduced himself as John Prince, a Swiss real estate developer. She told FOX 12 Oregon that she sensed something was wrong during their first date.

“It’s just awful, I can’t imagine how those women feel, I really can’t,” Anderson said after his arrest.

Anderson also described backlash for sharing her account and said she hoped speaking up would help others feel safe coming forward.

Propagate and Stardust Frames are behind the film, with North of Now and The Cut. The Way brothers, who created “Untold,” are part of the team. THR says a director and the people who will take part have yet to be named.

Love’s case is also headed toward trial. Oregon’s federal court calendar lists a jury trial for December 15. The charges remain allegations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
